Corporate Finance

Lecture 9 extras: Following finance day to day

Camilo Saldarriaga

Finance Department, ESCP Business School, 2026/2027

Why follow finance every day?

  • The ideas of this course (risk and return, the CAPM, market efficiency, capital structure) show up in the news every day: a firm borrows to buy back shares, a bank fails, a fund beats the market, or does not.

  • A few minutes a day with a good source turns the formulas into stories you remember, and teaches you the vocabulary of the people who work in finance.

  • Two free sources to start with:

    1. Unhedged, a podcast from the Financial Times.

    2. Money Stuff, a daily newsletter by Matt Levine at Bloomberg.

Unhedged: the FT markets podcast

  • A markets podcast from the Financial Times, every Tuesday and Thursday.

  • Hosted by Rob Armstrong and Katie Martin, FT markets journalists. They explain the big ideas behind what is happening in finance right now.

  • Free. Listen on:

    • Spotify

    • Apple Podcasts

    • Acast, or any podcast app: search “Unhedged”.

Money Stuff: Matt Levine’s newsletter

  • A column by Matt Levine at Bloomberg Opinion, sent by email every weekday. Deals, scandals and market oddities, explained clearly and with a lot of humour.

  • How to subscribe for free:

    1. Go to bloomberg.com/account/newsletters/money-stuff.

    2. Create a free Bloomberg account with your email address.

    3. Sign up to Money Stuff. The full column arrives in your inbox each weekday, even though most Bloomberg articles on the website are behind a paywall.

A story to follow: Anthropic’s IPO

  • IPO: a firm sells its shares to the public for the first time (Chap. 23.2, Lecture 11).

  • 26 October 2026: Anthropic filed its IPO document (S-1) with the SEC. Listing on the Nasdaq, ticker ANT. Price and size not yet set.

  • Last private value: $965bn (May 2026), up from $380bn in February.

  • Founders keep 50.1% of the votes: new shareholders get cash flows, little control.

Anthropic: the income statement

Source: Anthropic, PBC, Form S-1 filed with the SEC, 26 October 2026. Amounts in $ millions.

Anthropic: reading the numbers

  • Revenue explodes: $4.6bn in 2025, $33.2bn in nine months of 2026.

  • Operating loss shrinks: $8.1bn in 2025, $1.3bn in nine months of 2026. Biggest cost: compute.

  • Why a net loss of $104bn? $94.3bn comes from convertible notes (loans that can turn into shares). As the firm grew more valuable, they became worth more: an accounting loss, with no cash paid out.

  • Course link: about $417bn promised to compute providers. Fixed costs raise risk: operating leverage (Lecture 6).
